definitions.explanation: A person who has been physically injured, whether from an accident, disaster, or other incident. Used in news reports, emergency contexts, and everyday conversation about accidents.

examples.japanese: {怪我人|けがにん}はいませんか。
{事故|じこ}で3{人|にん}の{怪我人|けがにん}が{出|で}た。
examples.english: Three people were injured in the accident.

examples.japanese: {怪我人|けがにん}は{救急車|きゅうきゅうしゃ}で{病院|びょういん}に{運|はこ}ばれた。
examples.english: The injured person was taken to the hospital by ambulance.

examples.japanese: {幸|さいわ}い{怪我人|けがにん}は{出|で}なかったが、{建物|たてもの}の{被害|ひがい}は{大|おお}きかった。
examples.english: Fortunately there were no injuries, but the damage to the building was extensive.

notes:
Composed of {怪我|けが} (injury) and {人|にん} (person). The {人|にん} suffix is read にん (not じん) in this compound. The word is standard in news reports and emergency situations to describe anyone who has been physically hurt.

The phrase {怪我人|けがにん}が{出|で}る (injuries occurred; someone was hurt) is extremely common in news and accident reports. Its opposite — {怪我人|けがにん}は{出|で}なかった (no one was injured) — is equally standard when reporting the fortunate outcome of an incident.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {怪我人|けがにん}が{出|で}る: there are injuries / someone is injured
- {怪我人|けがにん}は{出|で}なかった: no one was injured
- {怪我人|けがにん}を{救助|きゅうじょ}する: to rescue the injured
- {怪我人|けがにん}を{運|はこ}ぶ: to transport the injured
- {重傷|じゅうしょう}の{怪我人|けがにん}: a seriously injured person

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {負傷者|ふしょうしゃ}: injured person — a more formal synonym, common in official reports and news
- {被害者|ひがいしゃ}: victim — broader term including injury, crime, or disaster victims
- {死傷者|ししょうしゃ}: casualties (dead and injured) — used when reporting both fatalities and injuries together
